title: Version Control Concepts
learningObjectives: Distinguish a repository from an ordinary folder.
Never commit credentials or treat Git as a backup.

understand.concept: Version control records changes over time. It helps inspect history, compare versions, restore earlier work, and coordinate collaboration. A repository stores tracked history; commits record snapshots; branches support separate lines of work. Version control is not a secret vault or a complete backup strategy.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear, repeatable practices help beginners make safe changes and understand how work moves from an idea to a checked result.
understand.analogy: A small checklist helps a person complete a task in order without forgetting important steps.
understand.analogyLimit: Software workflows also involve technical tools, dependencies, collaboration, and test evidence, which a checklist analogy cannot fully describe.

explain.narrative: Track intentional source changes, review diffs, and make coherent commits with useful messages. Avoid credentials, unrelated files, and generated clutter. A remote repository enables sharing but requires thoughtful permissions and backup practices.
